body: Looks like you can just `return true` here and below and get rid of the `handled` variable.
Can you turn `8.0f` into a constant with a comment to describe what it represents.
Does this account for drag & drop via mouse motion?

For mouse input, it's always true.

Edit: Hm.. I think it won't work if user switch between touch and mouse.

It's drag threshold, that a drag must exceed before triggering a scroll. It was to prevent accidental scroll but I've removed it now because the drag event already has some internal threshold. We also don't have any threshold in TextEdit.
Switching between mouse and touch is fixed now
Should this also be reset when we detect a mousemotion or mousebutton?

Shouldn't be needed because `can_start_drag_drop` is `true` by default and when switched from mouse to touch it becomes `false` on press and again `true` on release. So, when user switches from touch to mouse, `can_start_drag_drop` would be true at that point.
But I guess I can reset it for mouse event just for extra safety.

Edit: Ok, Logic wasn't setting `can_start_drag_drop` to true on long press release, so mouse drag after that wasn't working. Now It's reset on mouse button event. Seems to work as expected in my testing.
Already fixed in `long_press` PR. I just need to rebase.
